jobs.title: Preparador/a de oposiciones de Bibliotecas, Archivos y Museos (Auxiliar, Ayudant
jobs.excerpt: 🚀 Únete al claustro de preparadores de Polaris x Ucademy ¿Trabajas en una biblioteca, archivo o museo público, o preparas estas oposiciones?
jobs.description:
🚀 Únete al claustro de preparadores de Polaris x Ucademy

¿Trabajas en una biblioteca, archivo o museo público, o preparas estas oposiciones? Colabora en remoto con Polaris x Ucademy y ayuda a otros a conseguir su plaza.

📚 Buscamos preparadores/as para las oposiciones de Bibliotecas, Archivos y Museos

Queremos construir un claustro de preparadores especializados en Bibliotecas, Archivos y Museos, en el que cada profesional aporte su experiencia en su ámbito y en su nivel.

No necesitas dominar todas las categorías. Puedes especializarte en Bibliotecas, Archivos o Museos, y en uno o varios niveles: Auxiliar, Ayudante o Facultativo/Conservador.

🗂️ Oposiciones para las que buscamos preparadores

⭐ Auxiliares (C1 / C2)

  • Auxiliar de Bibliotecas

  • Auxiliar de Archivos

  • Auxiliar de Museos

Se convocan sobre todo en comunidades autónomas, ayuntamientos, diputaciones y universidades, con denominaciones y grupo que varían según la administración.

⭐ Ayudantes (A2)

  • Ayudantes de Bibliotecas

  • Ayudantes de Archivos

  • Ayudantes de Museos

En el Estado, Cuerpo de Ayudantes de Archivos, Bibliotecas y Museos. En otras administraciones, escalas equivalentes con su propia denominación.

Facultativos y Conservadores (A1)

  • Facultativos de Bibliotecas

  • Facultativos de Archivos

  • Conservadores de Museos

En el Estado, Cuerpo Facultativo de Archiveros, Bibliotecarios y Arqueólogos y Cuerpo Facultativo de Conservadores de Museos. En otras administraciones, escalas superiores equivalentes.

🏛️ Una misma profesión, muchas convocatorias

Estas oposiciones las convocan administraciones muy distintas, y cada una tiene su denominación, su temario y su forma de examinar. Buscamos preparadores que conozcan procesos selectivos de:

  • Administración General del Estado / Ministerio de Cultura

  • Comunidades Autónomas

  • Ayuntamientos y otras entidades locales

  • Diputaciones

  • Universidades públicas

  • Otros organismos públicos

En las convocatorias autonómicas, locales y universitarias, la normativa y los sistemas de cada territorio o institución marcan la diferencia. Por eso queremos contar con preparadores de todas las comunidades autónomas.

🌟 Quiénes somos

En Polaris x Ucademy preparamos oposiciones de una forma más digital, práctica y personalizada. Ya hemos acompañado a miles de opositores y tenemos un objetivo claro: que 10.000 personas consigan su plaza preparándose con nosotros.

Para lograrlo, estamos ampliando nuestro claustro de preparadores de alto rendimiento.

Somos muy digitales, pero lo humano no se negocia. La tecnología nos ayuda a enseñar mejor, y son nuestros preparadores quienes aportan conocimiento, criterio, cercanía y acompañamiento.

🔎 A quién buscamos

  • Profesionales con plaza (funcionarios/as o personal laboral fijo, en activo o en excedencia) en bibliotecas, archivos o museos públicos.

  • Preparadores/as con experiencia en estas oposiciones.

  • Personas capaces de trabajar las dos caras de la oposición:

    • el contenido técnico de la profesión (biblioteconomía, archivística, museología, gestión de colecciones, normalización…),

    • y la legislación y el contenido específico de la administración que convoca, incluida la normativa autonómica cuando corresponda.

  • Quienes dominen las pruebas prácticas: catalogación y clasificación, descripción archivística, documentación de fondos museográficos…

  • Quienes sepan enseñar y acompañar: explicar con claridad, dar feedback útil y ayudar a sostener la preparación.

  • Soltura con herramientas digitales. Si ya utilizas IA en tu día a día, mucho mejor.

🎯 En qué podrás colaborar

Según tu ámbito, tu nivel y tu disponibilidad, podrás participar en uno o varios proyectos:

  • Clases online del temario técnico y del temario específico de cada administración.

  • Supuestos prácticos: diseñarlos, resolverlos y corregir los de los alumnos.

  • Legislación de patrimonio, bibliotecas, archivos y museos, estatal y autonómica.

  • Preguntas tipo test y simulacros con el formato real.

  • Preparación de pruebas orales o de desarrollo, en los niveles superiores.

  • Seguimiento de alumnos: resolver dudas y ayudarles a avanzar.

  • Temarios, esquemas, resúmenes y vídeos cortos.

🤝 Cómo funciona la colaboración

No es un puesto de trabajo a jornada completa ni parcial. Colaborarás con Polaris x Ucademy mediante prestación de servicios en proyectos educativos concretos, compatible con tu actividad profesional.

Si tienes plaza, no te pedimos que dejes tu puesto. Queremos que pongas tu experiencia al servicio de otros opositores de una forma flexible.

🌍 100 % remoto
🕐 Horarios y disponibilidad a convenir
📚 Proyectos y entregables definidos desde el inicio
💰 Compensación competitiva según el proyecto y los entregables

🎬 Cómo es el proceso de selección

Queremos conocerte enseñando, no solo leyendo tu CV. El proceso tiene tres pasos:

1. Revisión de perfil. En la candidatura responderás a unas preguntas breves y nos enviarás un vídeo de presentación de 1 minuto. Grábalo con el móvil, sin complicaciones: cuéntanos quién eres, tu ámbito (bibliotecas, archivos o museos), tu nivel, en qué comunidad autónoma trabajas y qué administraciones conoces.

2. Contacto de validación. Si tu perfil encaja, nos pondremos en contacto contigo por llamada o por escrito para resolver dudas, conocer tu disponibilidad y explicarte cómo colaboramos.

3. Clase de prueba y entrevista. Agendarás tu entrevista y, antes de la fecha, nos enviarás una clase grabada de máximo 5 minutos: la explicación de un contenido del temario o la resolución de un supuesto práctico (por ejemplo, un ejercicio de catalogación o de descripción archivística), con un material de apoyo creado por ti. No buscamos una producción perfecta: queremos ver cómo explicas y cómo haces sencillo lo difícil.

Si conoces el camino hacia una plaza en bibliotecas, archivos o museos y quieres ayudar a otros a recorrerlo, queremos conocerte.

jobs.excerpt: NVIDIA DGX Cloud is the AI supercomputing-as-a-service substrate designed to power the next generation of AI and industrial-scale breakthroughs.
jobs.description:
NVIDIA DGX Cloud is the AI supercomputing-as-a-service substrate designed to power the next generation of AI and industrial-scale breakthroughs. As a Security Engineer within our Infrastructure Security Engineering organization, you will not just help "secure" our platform—you will architect and build the foundational security primitives that protect massive-scale GPU clusters. You will design automated, resilient security systems that help ensure the integrity of our omni-cloud and on-premise AI infrastructure.

What You Will Be Doing:

  • Security Engineering: Design, build, and integrate production-grade security services. You will focus on the engineering of security products—transforming third-party and open-source tools into seamless, API-driven components of the DGX Cloud security stack.

  • Automated Policy Enforcement: Shift security "left" by developing Infrastructure as Code and Policy as Code to automate security enforcement and compliance at the speed of cloud-scale deployment.

  • Orchestration Security & Guardrails: Architect and implement the security control plane. You will engineer automated guardrails, controllers, and runtime security policies that validate and enforce the integrity of tenant boundaries.

  • Security-as-a-Service Approach: Designing and operating security services as a scalable platform. Building "self-service" security primitives (e.g., Identity-as-a-Service, automated secrets management, and real-time scanning APIs) that allow developer teams to move fast.

  • Security Tooling & Lifecycle: Develop internal security frameworks and automated response systems. Responsible for the full software development lifecycle (SDLC) of the security tools, including testing, deployment, and maintenance.

  • Threat Modeling & System Design: Conduct deep-dive threat models on complex distributed systems and the DGX Cloud stack, identifying architectural gaps in security and engineering the solutions to close them.

  • Multi-Functional Collaboration: Partner with DGX Cloud platform teams, broader NVIDIA security teams, and product engineering to understand their needs and build paved paths that seamlessly embed security into the CI/CD pipeline and the hardware lifecycle.

What We Need to See:

We are looking for high-caliber engineers with deep spikes of expertise in a few of these areas and the intellectual curiosity to dive into the rest. If your experience aligns with the core of this role—building resilient security systems—and you can show us how, we want to hear from you!

  • Infrastructure Engineering: Experience (typically 8+ years) in SRE, Software Engineering, and Infrastructure Security. You focus on building systemic solutions rather than performing manual operations or "tool administration."

  • Production-Grade Coding: A strong software engineering background with the ability to write clean, maintainable, and well-tested code. You should be comfortable building and maintaining production service at scale.

  • Distributed Systems Expertise: Understanding of cloud-native architecture, container orchestration (Kubernetes), and the security challenges inherent in high-throughput, low-latency environments.

  • Platformizing Security: Transform complex security requirements into consumable internal services. You will focus on the "Developer Experience" of security, ensuring that our infrastructure security controls are delivered as robust, API-first platforms that integrate seamlessly with NVIDIA’s internal engineering workflows.

  • Security Product Integration: Proven track record of taking complex security products (AuthN/AuthZ, Vaulting, Scanning, IDS) and integrating them into an automated infrastructure via APIs and custom glue-code.

  • Linux Internals: Strong hands-on experience with Linux systems security, including kernel-level primitives (eBPF, AppArmor, or SELinux).

  • Foundation: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field (or equivalent experience).

Ways To Stand Out from the Crowd:

  • HPC/AI Security: Experience securing high-performance computing environments, RDMA-based networks, or GPU-specific security challenges.

  • Cloud-Native Identity: Expertise in workload identity frameworks (e.g., SPIFFE/SPIRE) and hardware-root-of-trust (TPM/HSM) integration.

  • Open Source Impact: Notable contributions to security-focused open-source projects or a track record of engineering-focused security research. How have you represented and helped advance the industry?

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary ranges for this position are:
170,000 CAD – 220,000 CAD for Level 4; and 225,000 CAD – 275,000 CAD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

The Global Payroll Operations Partner is responsible for the successful operational delivery, validation and oversight of assigned payrolls and legal entities. Acting as the primary operational owner for a portfolio of payrolls, countries and entities, this role ensures payrolls are delivered accurately, compliantly and on time through effective payroll validation, issue resolution, stakeholder management and vendor management.

The Payroll Operations Partner works closely with HR Service Delivery, Finance, Reward, Benefits, Technology teams and external payroll providers to deliver a seamless payroll experience while maintaining strong controls, compliance and operational excellence.

As the payroll function continues to evolve, this role will increasingly leverage data, automation, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies to improve payroll outcomes, enhance employee experience and generate business insights.

This role reports to the Payroll Manager.

Payroll Portfolio Ownership

  • Act as the operational owner for assigned payrolls, countries and legal entities.
  • Maintain accountability for payroll delivery and operational outcomes within assigned payroll portfolios.
  • Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders and payroll providers.
  • Manage payroll-related risks, dependencies and operational issues.
  • Escalate significant risks or service issues appropriately.

Data Quality & Exception Management

  • Investigate payroll-impacting data issues and discrepancies.
  • Monitor integration exceptions and payroll-related data issues.
  • Partner with HR Service Delivery and other stakeholders to resolve root causes.
  • Identify recurring data quality concerns and support long-term resolution.

Vendor & Service Management

  • Act as the primary operational contact for payroll providers supporting assigned payrolls.

  • Support operational vendor reviews and improvement discussions.
  • Escalate service delivery concerns through established governance channels.

Employee & Stakeholder Support

About National Council of Urban Indian Health

The National Council of Urban Indian Health (NCUIH) was founded to represent the interests of Urban Indian Organizations (UIOs) before Congress and Federal agencies and influence policies impacting the health conditions experienced by urban American Indians and Alaska Natives (AI/ANs). NCUIH is a 501(c)(3), membership-based organization devoted to supporting the development of quality, accessible, and culturally sensitive healthcare programs for AI/ANs living in urban communities. NCUIH provides advocacy, education, training, and leadership for urban Indian healthcare providers and represents UIOs funded through Title V of the Indian Health Care Improvement Act and the AI/ANs they serve.

Position Summary

The Director of Communications & Events (Director) leads NCUIH's communications function and provides strategic oversight of its annual conference of more than 300 participants and other assigned events. The Director manages staff, leads editorial priorities, digital platforms and communications deliverables across NCUIH's grants and organizational priorities. The Director supervises communications staff and an Events Manager, who is responsible for day-to-day planning and execution of the conference and other NCUIH events. Working under the direction of the Sr. VP of Policy & Communications, the Director sets priorities, delegates responsibilities, monitors budgets and milestones, and ensures communications and events advance NCUIH's mission.

Duties and Responsibilities

Communications leadership and public engagement

  • Develop and maintain an integrated communications and editorial calendar covering grant products, policy priorities, newsletters, organizational announcements, publications, digital content and events.
  • Supervise communications and events staff and coordinate graphic design, website, social media, newsletter, video and podcast production; allocate work and manage external production support.
  • Maintain NCUIH's brand, editorial standards and communications procedures; lead editing and quality review of public-facing materials and route technical, policy and executive approvals.
  • Develop leadership presentations, talking points, speeches, media materials and public relations campaigns assigned by the Sr. VP of Policy & Communications and CEO.
  • Manage press outreach and inquiries as assigned. Manage website and resource-library updates, email marketing and social media.
  • Monitor audience engagement, maintain accurate distribution lists and improve access to NCUIH resources.
  • Maintain professional engagement with national partners, stakeholders, and advocates and foster strong relationships with key national and regional contacts.

Staff supervision and team management

  • Provide direct supervision, coaching and performance feedback to communications staff and the Events Manager; establish clear responsibilities, goals and deadlines.
  • Manage team capacity and coordinate assignments across communications and events; use shared project plans to track deliverables, internal reviews and dependencies.
  • Support staff development and evaluate performance; resolve workload or execution concerns and elevate decisions requiring senior leadership approval.
  • Oversee processes, procedures and workflows of communications and events.

Grant Communications and Dissemination

  • Translate approved workplans into a production schedule with content owners, review deadlines, design needs, publication dates and dissemination measures across new and existing grants.
  • Lead the communications work for the HRSA HIV project, including the design, production, and promotion of HIV webpages, the resource library and learning platform, fact sheets, clinical guides, educational videos, training announcements, and needs-assessment publications, using substantive content developed by program staff and subject matter experts.
  • Coordinate Office of Minority Health (OMH) communications and language-access planning with TARC.
  • Lead the design, production, and promotion of OMH project materials such as prevention materials, the toolkit, UIO snapshots, SME examples, website resources, audio or virtual products and lessons learned materials, using substantive content developed by program staff and subject matter experts.
  • Manage design and dissemination of funded Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) and (Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAI) guidance, training resources and project findings through webpages, newsletters, direct UIO outreach and other approved channels.
  • Working with TARC staff, ensure materials receive appropriate technical and cultural review and meet plain-language and accessibility standards; coordinate translation, captions, transcripts, alternate formats and consent for identifiable stories and media.
  • Lead efforts to compile communications outputs and reach data, including publication records, distribution, webpage use, email engagement, media views and event participation, for grant reporting and improvement.

Conference planning and event implementation

  • Supervise the Events Manager, who is responsible for the integrated event workplan and day-to-day execution of the annual conference and other assigned events, including logistics, vendors, registration, production, accessibility, volunteers and onsite delivery.
  • Set event goals and priorities; review the Event Manager’s workplans, deliverables, milestones, budget tracking and readiness reports, resolve implementation issues and route procurement, contract and financial approvals to Partnerships and Operations.
  • Lead conference marketing, website and agenda publication, speaker materials, signage, attendee communications and the onsite run of show.
  • Coordinate content approval with the CEO, TARC and Policy & Communications, while the Events Manager manages the operational run of show and onsite execution.
  • Ensure the Events Manager partners with the Development Department to execute the conference; integrate fundraising and partnership milestones, sponsor and exhibitor commitments, recognition and fulfillment into the master plan.
  • Lead communications, production and timelines for other assigned webinars, trainings, regional institutes, receptions and convenings.
  • Supervises the Events Manager on operational planning, vendors, platforms, accessibility, logistics and participant follow-up; supervises and assigns tasks to communications staff on promotion and content production.
  • Lead joint planning meetings and post-conference debriefs with the Director of Development and other departments; review results and the Events Manager’s recommendations, coordinate financial reconciliation with the Director of Finance and ensure improvements are implemented.
  • Other communications tasks and events duties as assigned.

Requirements and Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in communications, journalism, marketing, public relations, event management or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.
  • At least six (6) years of progressively responsible communications experience, managing complex projects or communications production teams.
  • At least two (2) years' experience directly supervising staff, including assigning work and providing performance feedback.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage editorial planning, digital communications, publications, media relations, and simultaneous deadlines.
  • Experience leading planning and implementation of a complex, multi-day conference or comparable event, including budgets, vendors, cross-functional teams and onsite delivery.
  • Demonstrated ability to delegate execution and hold staff accountable for results.
  • Excellent writing, editing, judgment, and quality control skills.
  • Ability to translate public health or policy information for different audiences.
  • Working proficiency with Microsoft 365, project management systems, website content management, email marketing, virtual event tools, and design collaboration tools.
  • Commitment to culturally responsive communication and ability to work respectfully with UIOs and American Indian and Alaska Native communities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's degree, or equivalent advanced professional experience in communications or a related field.

NCUIH Team Member Perks

jobs.description:
NikoHealth is a rapidly growing SaaS company transforming how Durable Medical Equipment (DME) and Home Medical Equipment (HME) providers operate. Our innovative, all-in-one platform streamlines business operations, empowering providers to work smarter and more efficiently.

About The Role

This is a newly created role, and one of the first two engineering hires NikoHealth will made in the United States. You'll report directly to the CTO and own how our software gets released and run while working closely with other senior engineers.

We operate dozens of .NET services deployed per-customer on Windows Server and IIS in AWS, managed with Terraform and Octopus Deploy. Across hundreds of provider tenants that's thousands of running application instances. Today a change waits for the next release train, and the train then takes weeks to reach the whole fleet, so end-to-end a given feature takes months. Improving our deployment and development experience is the first job. After that there are dozens of areas of platform investment needed to support how fast we're scaling.

What You'll Do

  • Own our CI/CD pipeline end to end, with the authority to change what it deploys and how.
  • Own developer experience. Reproducible builds, a local environment someone can actually stand up, and fast honest feedback on every change. This is half the job, not a side effect of the other half.
  • Get our automated regression suite running in CI. It exists, it's substantial, and it isn't currently executed.
  • Cut release lead time and get the fleet inside a published, committed release window.
  • Make fleet version state answerable by a query instead of by a person, so anyone can see what a customer is running.
  • Design and publish an access model, so provisioning stops routing through one inbox.
  • Start bringing runtimes and dependencies current, beginning with the shared libraries everything else depends on.
  • Document and share what you learn, so infrastructure knowledge stops being concentrated in one place.

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years in platform, infrastructure, or DevOps engineering.
  • Production Terraform, including state you owned and drift you had to reconcile.
  • Production Windows Server and IIS, application pools included.
  • End-to-end ownership of a CI/CD pipeline in a previous role.
  • AWS at the level this estate uses it: EC2, ALB, VPC, IAM.
  • A track record of replacing a manual process with a measured and automated one, where you can tell us the before and after.
  • Evidence you've made other engineers faster, not just the systems. Build times, local setup, test feedback, whatever it was.
  • Daily working use of AI coding agents such as Cursor or Claude Code, including the harness around them: tests, project instructions, and a loop you can run again.

Nice to have

  • Octopus Deploy, or another deployment orchestrator you owned.
  • Single-tenant or multi-tenant SaaS at meaningful scale.
  • Healthcare, HIPAA, or another regulated environment.

How we work

This is brownfield and we're honest about it. Some of this estate is well-built and some of it grew. We're not asking you to rewrite it, because hundreds of providers bill claims through it every day. We're asking you to make it measurable, make it safe to change, then change it. If you've built a career inheriting other people's systems and making them boring, you'll like it here.

We work with AI agents, seriously. The team works agentically and so will you. What matters is what you do after the agent produces something: tests, linters, project instructions, a loop you can run again. If your answer to a bad result is a longer prompt, we're probably not a fit. This is also why developer experience sits in this role rather than somewhere else: an agent is only as good as the feedback loop it runs in, and ours needs work.

Most application development is done by a long-standing engineering partner. You'd own the pipeline, the infrastructure, and the environments, and over time the standards their code meets before it ships while working closely with our off-shore development team.

Two people isn't a platform team, it's the start of one. Until it's three, coverage is shared between you, the CTO, and our head of engineering. Everyone here is remote, and we'd like your hours to overlap the US East Coast.

This is the start of the engineering team, not the end of it. We're hiring more engineers through 2027. The people who join first get the widest scope, the most say in how the team gets built, and first choice about what they own as it grows.

How to apply

Apply through the link on this page. Instead of a cover letter, we ask one question: tell us about a system you inherited, and the first thing you measured. A few sentences is plenty.

Use AI to help write your application if you want to, we do too. We read every one ourselves, and we can tell when nobody read the posting.

Your first conversation will be with our CTO, who is the hiring manager and will walk you through the rest of the process.

Compensation and benefits

Sí te gusta estar rodeado de buen@s compañer@s, trabajar con buen rollo y en un ambiente colaborativo ¡sigue leyendo! seguro que idealista te va a gustar 😉

¿Qué harás?

  • Trabajarás junto a tus compañer@s del equipo desarrollando nuevas funcionalidades.
  • Tendrás un trato fluido con la gente de negocio para poder entender sus necesidades y problemas. Además, trabajarás codo con codo con nuestro equipo de producto y UX para aportar una visión técnica a las soluciones que definamos para los mismos.
  • Ayudarás a que la plataforma esté estable…Sí, en idealista también tenemos bugs, así que tendrás que ayudar a identificarlos y solucionarlos.

¿Qué te ofrecemos?

  • Podrás ver el impacto directo de tu trabajo en una de las webs de referencia tanto en España, como en Italia y Portugal. Para los que no lo hayáis vivido ya: no sabéis el cosquilleo que da en la tripa la primera vez que ves algo que has hecho en una plataforma que utilizan millones de personas.
  • Somos Remote Friendly :) pero tenemos oficinas en el centro de Madrid para vernos de vez en cuando.
  • Vas a aprender. Lo decimos en serio. La plataforma va evolucionando constantemente, y de ahí sacamos mogollón de charlas internas, posts, talleres… que hacen que el conocimiento fluya.
  • Además... patrocinamos eventos, acudimos a ellos y hacemos muchos meetups. ¡Es tan importante aprender como enseñar a tus compis!
  • Además de tu salario, podrás acogerte a un plan de retribución flexible (tarjeta de transporte, cheques gourmet, seguro médico…) del que te podrás beneficiar desde el primer día.
  • Clases de Inglés, italiano y portugués.
  • Fruta fresca y café siempre disponible en la cocina.
  • ¡También tenemos fisio y clases de yoga … porque para nosotros lo más importante es cuidar de nuestros idealistas!
  • Además de trabajar, nos gusta pasarlo bien, por eso que si te unes a nuestra familia, cada mes celebrarás algo…Halloween, San Valentín, Navidad,…¡Te lo vas a pasar muy bien!
  • Teambuilding y mucho más!

¿Qué esperamos de ti?

  • Tienes al menos 3 años de experiencia desarrollando el backend de alguna aplicación utilizando Java, y nos puedes hablar de ello.
  • Nosotr@s trabajamos principalmente con Java y Spring pero lo que de verdad nos interesa es que tengas ciertos fundamentos de programación bien asentados.
  • No te quedas en el “con que funcione vale”. Nosotr@s damos mucho valor tanto a las buenas prácticas, como a definir diseños y arquitecturas que nos permitan extender la plataforma de manera sostenible. Así que esperamos que estos sean términos a los que tú también les des importancia.
  • Nosotr@s trabajamos en equipo. El equipo son tus compañer@s; pero también lo es la gente de producto y UX, así como la gente de negocio, etc.

  • Tienes curiosidad e iniciativa. Al final, este trabajo va de los problemas que somos capaces de resolver y de cómo logramos hacerlo. Así que se espera de ti que seas capaz de analizar, preguntar, pedir ayuda (y ofrecerla), y saber plantear soluciones a los mismos.

¿Qué otras cosas son un plus?

Position Summary

As ICU Medical transitions to Workday, this role will support the implementation, stabilization, and ongoing evolution of the Workday platform. The analyst will bring depth in one or more Workday modules (such as HCM) and apply that expertise across other modules and functional areas as business needs and priorities change. Working under the direction of the Workday Program Manager, the HRIS Manager and senior project team members, this position will partner with functional HR and business leaders to gather requirements, configure and test solutions, validate data, and ensure business needs are accurately reflected in Workday. The role will also support post-go-live needs and the broader Workday roadmap, and will work with the primary reporting owner to ensure reporting needs are met and no business gaps are created with the deployment.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Workday Implementation & Support

  • Support the implementation of Workday across the HR platform, with an area of focus in one or more modules (such as HCM), and extend support to other modules and functional areas as needed.

  • Partner with HR and business stakeholders to gather, document, and validate requirements, and translate them into configuration specifications.

  • Configure and test Workday functionality, including business process definitions, condition rules, notifications, and approval workflows.

  • Support data validation by reviewing and confirming that data loaded into Workday is complete and accurate, and by identifying and reporting discrepancies to the data conversion team for resolution.

  • Partner with the test administrator to ensure test scenarios are fully built out, accurately reflect business requirements and configuration, and are ready for execution; support system integration testing, user acceptance testing, and parallel testing, and track and resolve test defects.

  • Support Workday security configuration, ensuring appropriate access to data and alignment with privacy and compliance requirements.

  • Support additional Workday modules, processes, and initiatives as business needs and priorities evolve.

Reporting Support

  • Partner with the primary Workday reporting owner to communicate reporting requirements and ensure current-state reporting needs are met at go-live.

  • Run audit and reconciliation reports to support data validation, confirming that all data from legacy systems was loaded accurately into Workday during validation cycles and after go-live.

  • Provide subject matter input on report data sources, security, and field definitions, and support basic ad hoc reporting needs as directed.

Post Go-Live & Platform Roadmap Support

  • Provide post-go-live support and stabilization, including troubleshooting transactions, resolving data issues, triaging and tracking open issues and enhancement requests, and responding to HR and employee inquiries.

  • Support the broader Workday platform roadmap by gathering and assessing HR and business needs, documenting requirements, and helping prioritize enhancements and future-phase deployments across modules.

  • Partner with the HRIS team and the Workday project team to plan, configure, and test roadmap items, ensuring changes are well documented and aligned with the overall platform strategy.

Team & Platform Partnership

  • Support Workday bi-annual releases by assessing potential impacts to Workday functionality, conducting regression testing, and implementing required updates.

  • Collaborate closely with the HRIS team, the Workday project team, the reporting owner, and integration and functional leads on configuration changes and enhancements that affect Workday data and processes.

  • Contribute to documentation, standards, naming conventions, and training materials.

  • Advise on data quality, governance, and audit readiness for Workday data.

Knowledge & Skills

  • Strong working knowledge of at least one Workday module (such as HCM, Absence, Benefits, Time, Compensation, Recruiting, or Talent), with the ability and willingness to learn and support additional modules.
  • Experience validating data loaded into Workday, including reconciling source data to Workday reports.
  • Working knowledge of Workday reporting tools and calculated fields sufficient to validate data and support the reporting owner.
  • Ability to gather and translate business requirements into clear, scalable configuration solutions and to support a long-term platform roadmap.
  • Strong ability to prioritize work, manage time independently, and follow through on tasks.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Basic project management skills, including scoping work, planning tasks, and communicating progress.
  • This role involves interaction and collaboration with other departments and requires excellent judgment and interpersonal skills.
  • Natural self-starter and creative problem solver with a continuous improvement mindset.

Minimum Qualifications, Education & Experience

  • Must be at least 18 years of age.

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Human Resources, Business, Information Systems, or related field, or equivalent relevant work experience, is preferred.

  • 6+ years of hands-on Workday experience in a production environment; Workday implementation and post-go-live support experience preferred.
  • Working knowledge of Workday module configuration and business processes in one or more areas. Workday certification in a relevant module preferred.
  • Working knowledge of Workday Security concepts including domain and business process security policies and security groups.
  • Working knowledge of Workday reporting, including report fields and calculated fields.

Work Environment

  • This is largely a sedentary role.

  • Typically requires travel less than 5% of the time.

About us:

Braveheart Bio is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing therapies for patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and other serious cardiovascular diseases. Our lead product candidate, BHB-1893, is a next-generation oral small-molecule cardiac myosin inhibitor (CMI) being developed for the treatment of obstructive HCM (oHCM) and non-obstructive HCM (nHCM). Braveheart’s goal is to improve the treatment options for these patients by enhancing speed of onset, depth of gradient response, systolic safety, reversibility and reducing prescribing complexity.

This role requires an energetic self-starter who excels at cross-functional coordination, thrives under tight deadlines, and possesses sharp proposal writing and architecture skills.


The day-to-day

  • Capture Execution & Planning: Partner with the assigned BD lead to operationalize and execute structured capture strategies for assigned opportunities, including capture planning, gate readiness, cross-functional coordination, solution maturity, and proposal transition.

  • Status Reporting: Maintain robust documentation and provide clear status reporting on pursuit health and proposal progress to Win Center leadership and executive stakeholders.
  • Solicitation Analysis: Conduct comprehensive reviews of federal solicitations (RFPs, RFIs, RFQs) to perform requirements analysis and standard/custom solution mapping.

Professional Profile

  • Detail-Oriented Operator: You are an organized self-starter who can multi-task, prioritize assignments under tight timelines, and maintain strict accuracy under pressure.

What you'll need

  • Experience: 10+ years leading federal proposal efforts with demonstrated experience supporting capture planning, win strategy, and pre-RFP activities – or equivalent capture experience with strong proposal execution capability.

  • CRM & Publishing Tools: Familiarity with CRM systems and desktop publishing applications, including the Adobe Creative Cloud suite (InDesign, Illustrator).

Department:Policy

FLSA Status:Exempt

Project End Date: March 31, 2029

Why We’re Here

“No one working full time in the richest country on Earth should have to choose between a doctor’s visit and dinner on the table. But that’s exactly what happens when we treat health care like a luxury instead of a right.” Community Catalyst is seeking Senior Policy Analyst to help shape the national conversation on health justice and elevate the organization’s role as a leading authority on equitable health systems in the United States.

About Community Catalyst

Community Catalyst is the national health justice organization working to ensure care is accessible, affordable, and accountable to the people it serves—and that racial bias does not determine who receives care. For more than two decades, Community Catalyst has partnered with state and community advocates to change systems before harm occurs. The organization integrates policy reform, community organizing, data science, narrative strategy, and thought leadership to advance structural change in health care.

The Opportunity

The Senior Policy Analyst provides leadership, strategic advice, policy analysis, and contributes to the creation of policy resources to translate information to health advocates, providers and policymakers. The Senior Policy Analyst supports issues related to healthcare access and affordability, with a particular focus on eliminating disparities faced by low-income populations and communities of color through power building, advocacy, teaching and learning.

The Senior Policy Analyst works as part of a team to offer policy analysis, strategic insight, and support to state consumer health advocates and grassroots partners. The Senior Policy Analyst will also help lead initiatives to support national and state partners and advocacy coalitions in pursuing their policy advocacy goals.

Responsibilities

  • Track and analyze state-level legislation, regulations, and other policies impacting health coverage and affordability, with a particular focus on Medicaid; synthesize trends across states and identify points of connection to federal policy activity.
  • Build and maintain relationships with state and community-based partners and provide them with policy research and analysis and strategic guidance on how to defend and advance health coverage and affordability across a range of issue areas; adapt resources and information to specific state context and policy environments.
  • Draft comment letters, issue briefs, fact sheets, blogs, and reports on pertinent health policy topics to support the organization, as well as state and national partners.
  • Help craft and implement the organization’s state and federal policy agenda in collaboration with the senior policy staff.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with collaborating national and state organizations, including assisting with development and operationalization of any shared deliverables.
  • Develop sufficient expertise in a number of policy areas that are part of the agenda and the broader Community Catalyst health policy agenda (e.g., medical debt, universal coverage models, health equity, caregiving and aging) to help connect the dots across issue areas for Community Catalyst and state partners.
  • Coordinate and collaborate with other Community Catalyst programs on cross-cutting issues.
  • Support the development of grant and other funding proposals, including tracking of deliverables.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree plus at least 4 years of relevant work experience; or at least 7 years of relevant work experience
  • Broad, diverse knowledge and experience in state or federal health policy, including but not limited to legislative and regulatory issues related to Medicaid coverage, payment reform, health insurance markets, and health workforce.
  • Demonstrated ability to convey complex information in writing and orally so that it is easily understood by various audiences, including health advocacy partners and policymakers.
  • Demonstrated communication skills with ability to provide policy and advocacy coaching, technical assistance and capacity building to advocates in person and on the phone.
  • Experience advocating for local, state or federal policy or systems change.
  • Experience and knowledge of state and federal political processes and their interface with health policy.
  • Demonstrated history of working with a broad range of stakeholders including but not limited to policy advocates, grassroots advocates, community members, and decision makers.
  • An interest in and capacity for translating evidence-based research and knowledge into public policy strategies and practice
  • Organizational skills, including the ability to manage multiple tasks at once, respond to tight timelines, pay attention to detail, and operate effectively in a fast-paced environment
  • Demonstrated commitment to health equity and racial justice.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Ability to travel in US
  • Experience with state legislative health policy campaigns
  • Expertise in one or more state Medicaid systems
  • Experience working with patient and/or community-based advocacy organizations
  • Experience with public speaking, training, facilitating, and/or coaching
  • Lived experience in one ormore of the health issues listed on the Community Catalyst website
  • Bilingual/bicultural background

Supervisory Responsibilities

No supervisory responsibilities at this time.

Work Environment & Physical Requirements

This is a remote, office-based position performed from a home or remote workspace using standard office equipment and technology. Occasional travel may be required based on organizational needs. The role involves extended periods of sitting, regular computer use, and virtual communication. jobs.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Job Summary

Leads and manages team responsible for medical economics trend analysis activities and cost of care(CoC) initiative development, implementation, and measurement. Collaborates with health plans to identify and develop CoC initiatives and identify opportunities for trend mitigation and MLR improvement. Extracts and analyzes data from various sources to identify risks and opportunities, improve financial performance, and guide and influence decision-making related to clinical programs and operations.

Essential Job Duties

  • Analyzes medical claims and revenue trends to identify areas of concern and partners with health plan to develop mitigation strategies.
    • Identifies, models, and presents CoC initiatives to health plan for approval and partners with health plan leadership on implementation plan.
    • Represents medical economics department in cross-departmental and operational meetings.
    • Collaborates with and provides medical economics subject matter expertise for health plans and enterprise teams.
    • Creates reporting for strategic analysis, profitability, financial analysis, utilization patterns and medical management.
    • Reviews medical economics analysis work products to ensure accuracy and clarity.
    • Collects, validates, analyzes, and organizes data into meaningful reports for leadership decision making, and designs, develops, tests and deploys reports to other end users for operational and strategic analysis.
    • Provides oversight for medical economics team and activities - ensuring delivery of work/project plans and required reporting.
    • Recruits, hires, onboards, mentors, develops, and manages medical economics staff.
    • Provides daily management of data management, tools and technology work streams.
    • Facilitates workload distribution of new reports and project requests.
    • Coordinates with medical economics team to meet data analysis and database development needs.
    • Reviews, evaluates, and improves business logic and data sources.
    • Acts as a resource to team for medical economics/analysis related questions.
    • Serves as liaison between IT and medical economics for reporting needs.

Required Qualifications

  • At least 7 years of health care analytics and/or medical economics experience, preferably in claims processing environment and/or health care environment, or equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
    • At least 1 year of management/leadership experience.
    • Bachelor’s degree in statistics, mathematics, economics, computer science, health care management or related field.
    • Demonstrated understanding of Medicaid and Medicare programs or other health care plans.
    • Analytical work experience within the health care industry (i.e., hospital, network, ancillary, medical facility, health care vendor, commercial health insurance, large physician practice, managed care organization, etc.)
    • Strong knowledge of SQL queries and Power BI report development.
    • Familiar with relational database concepts, and SDLC concepts.
    • Proficiency with retrieving specified information from data sources.
    • Experience with building dashboards in Excel, Power BI, and/or Tableau and data management.
    • Knowledge of health care operations (utilization management, disease management, HEDIS quality measures, claims processing, etc.)
    • Knowledge of health care financial terms (e.g., PMPM, revenue) and different standard code systems (ICD-10CM, CPT, HCPCS, NDC, etc.) utilized in medical coding/billing (UB04/1500 form).
    • Demonstrated understanding of key managed care concepts and provider reimbursement principles such as risk adjustment, capitation, FFS (Fee-for-Service), Diagnosis Related Groups (DRG’s), Ambulatory Patient Groups (APG’s), Ambulatory Payment Classifications (APC’s), and other payment mechanisms.
    • Understanding of value-based risk arrangements
    • Experience in quantifying, measuring, and analyzing financial, operational, and/or utilization metrics in health care.
    • Ability to mine and manage information from large data sources.

• Demonstrated problem-solving skills.

  • Strong critical-thinking and attention to detail.
    • Ability to effectively collaborate with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
    • Strong time-management skills, and ability to manage simultaneous projects and tasks to meet internal deadlines.
    • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
    • Proficient in Microsoft Office suite products, key skills in Excel (VLOOKUPs and pivot tables)/applicable software program(s) proficiency.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in a health plan claims processing environment.
    • Experience developing and maintaining Power BI reports and dashboards.
    • Knowledge of relational database concepts and data structures.
    • Familiarity with Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) methodologies and processes.
    • Experience building analytical dashboards and visualizations using Tableau.
    • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related quantitative field.
    • Experience analyzing healthcare financial metrics such as PMPM, utilization trends, revenue, and cost drivers.
    • Advanced experience translating complex healthcare data into actionable insights for business stakeholders.
    • Experience supporting Medicaid and/or Medicare analytics in a managed care environment.
    • Experience working with large healthcare datasets including claims, membership, provider, quality, and utilization data.

We’re a place for people who are curious, bold, and motivated by meaningful work. Here, you'll have the opportunity to make an impact, explore new possibilities, and grow your career in ways that align with your interests and goals. When you're ready to take on something new, you'll find leaders who support your development and help you turn your ambition into action.


What you'll do

The Service Assurance Systems (SAS) Group, part of Global Operations, develop and maintain many software systems and applications which support the operation of Viasat services.

The team collects assurance and operational data from a wide range of systems across the Viasat estate. This data is shared between internal platforms and distributed through Google Cloud Platform (GCP), where it underpins observability and monitoring capabilities that give operations teams real-time insight into service health and performance. To ensure the data is accurate and fit for purpose, the team builds and maintains data pipelines that cleanse, transform and enrich raw data, making it readily consumable by our stakeholders across operations, engineering and management.

As a Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), you will play a key role in bridging the gap between software development and operational reliability. You will be responsible for supporting the applications built and maintained by the SAS group, managing deployments, investigating operational issues, and driving the team’s transition toward a modern DevOps culture. You will act as a first point of contact for service issues raised through the ServiceNow ticketing system, working to diagnose, triage and resolve incidents efficiently while collaborating closely with developers and operations teams.


The day-to-day

You will be working as part of a small team of developers and operations engineers, supporting the evolution of Viasat’s network and service monitoring capabilities, ensuring it remains world class in support of existing and future services.

Day-to-day the role will involve:

  • Investigate and resolve incidents, service requests and problems raised through the ServiceNow ticketing system, ensuring timely and thorough resolution within agreed SLAs.
  • Manage and oversee application deployments across development, staging and production environments, ensuring smooth and reliable release processes.
  • Monitor application and infrastructure health using observability tools such as Prometheus and AWS CloudWatch; proactively identify and respond to anomalies and performance degradation.
  • Own and maintain CI/CD pipelines, working to improve build, test and deployment automation to reduce manual effort and increase release confidence.
  • Champion and drive the adoption of DevOps practices and culture within the SAS group, working towards greater automation, infrastructure-as-code, and operational maturity.
  • Manage and maintain containerised workloads using Docker, and support the operation of services hosted on AWS cloud infrastructure.
  • Write and maintain operational scripts (primarily Python) to automate routine tasks, support incident investigations and improve team efficiency.
  • Collaborate with software developers to identify recurring operational issues and feed findings back into the development process to improve application resilience.
  • Maintain clear and up-to-date operational documentation including runbooks, deployment guides and incident post-mortems.
  • Provide written and verbal progress updates on open incidents, deployments and operational improvements to the SAS group and wider stakeholders.
  • Support on-call and out-of-hours incident response as required.
  • Liaise with engineering and infrastructure teams to ensure system changes are communicated and operationally risk-assessed before deployment.

What you'll need

  • Familiarity with both Windows and Linux operating systems, including command-line administration and troubleshooting.
  • Demonstrable experience with SQL or data pipeline technologies.
  • Experience with data processing frameworks such as Apache Airflow, Apache Flink or Google Dataflow, with a practical understanding of ETL pipeline design and the ability to diagnose issues across data transformation and scheduling workflows.
  • Demonstrable CI/CD experience — building, maintaining and improving pipelines using tools such as Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions or equivalent.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS services (e.g. EC2, S3, ECS, Lambda, CloudWatch) and containerisation using Docker.
  • Experience with monitoring and observability tooling, including Prometheus and AWS CloudWatch, for metrics collection, alerting and dashboarding.
  • Proficiency in scripting with Python for automation, tooling and operational support tasks.
  • Strong communication skills — able to clearly articulate technical issues and their impact to both technical and non-technical audiences, and to provide timely updates on incident progress.
  • Experience using an ITSM/ticketing system (e.g. ServiceNow) for incident management, request fulfilment and problem tracking.
  • A proactive, solution-oriented approach with strong attention to detail and a commitment to operational excellence.
  • A reasonable understanding and appreciation of IT and security standard methodologies in an operational environment.

What will help you on the job

  • Understanding of TCP/IP networking principles, including the ability to diagnose connectivity issues and interpret network traffic.
  • Familiarity with event streaming platforms such as Apache Kafka, including an understanding of producer/consumer patterns and how message queues are used to move data reliably between systems at scale.
  • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform or Ansible.
  • Experience with log aggregation and analysis platforms such as the OTEL Stack or AWS CloudWatch Logs Insights.
  • Exposure to Kubernetes or other container orchestration platforms.
  • Experience working in an Agile or DevOps team environment.

Who are we?
We are a female-founded scale-up, currently made up of around 100 AltoVitians. Our fully-remote team hails from 26 different countries and collectively speaks 29 languages. Most of the time, it is our differences that are celebrated (whether they are in cultures, personalities, preferences or passions). However, despite those differences, there are a few principal attributes that we share which define an AltoVitian. AltoVitians are tenacious, humble, and thoughtful. Being humble is important because it enables us to keep learning every day, and tenacity is necessary because in a high performing environment as fast-paced as AltoVita, taking it slow is simply not an option!

Today is a particularly exciting time to join our team, we closed our Series A financing round in late 2022 and will be starting the Series B rounds in the coming year. This next chapter won’t always be a smooth ride, but it will be filled with innovation, excitement and opportunities, so if you are ready for the challenge (and the fun!) of growing with us, we would love to hear from you.

What we do

AltoVita is a multi-award winning accommodation platform that enables enterprises to consolidate accommodation programmes through the power of proprietary technology paired with a human centric approach.

AltoVita’s unique offering sets us apart in the market, providing a network of 10 million+ verified and vetted properties are all duty of care compliant, backed by a four-tier quality control process; located in over 35,000 cities & 165 countries world-wide. With our award-winning enterprise software and human-centric approach, we deliver smart and sustainable solutions to global talent mobility & business travel managers worldwide.

Our Client Development team plays a vital role as trusted advisors and partners to our clients. Embodying our consultative philosophy, this dedicated team proactively shares new market insights, analyzes data, and empowers our clients with the tools and knowledge to make informed decisions, ensuring our clients are always equipped to make the best choices for their corporate housing needs.

AltoVita’s technology provides a cloud-based bridge between the highly fragmented property distribution system and multinational Global 2000 companies. A proprietary two-way API integration with a standardised sourcing process reduces the legacy, inefficient 48-to-72-hour bidding process down to a few minutes, saving valuable time and money.

Corporate clients love the bespoke user interface seamlessly configured to their mobility policies, and employees enjoy a greater sense of choice and support in their relocation journey.

  • Drive finance process improvements and automation where appropriate.

  • Collaborate with AltoVita’s Product team to ensure governance and compliance across new product releases

  • At least one year of industry experience.

Skills & Experience

jobs.description:
About Us

We are a modern marketing collective built for scale, efficiency, and impact. As the parent company, Agital supports three specialized agencies: Go Fish Digital, REQ, and WDG, with shared infrastructure, advanced technology, and deeply experienced people, allowing each brand to do its best work.

Go Fish Digital is an engineering-forward performance marketing agency specializing in SEO, Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), its Barracuda AI platform, social commerce, and conversion-focused creative.

WDG designs and builds complex enterprise web experiences for associations, nonprofits, foundations, universities, and other mission-driven organizations.

REQ is a digital marketing and communications agency specializing in brand, reputation, and advocacy for global organizations across technology, healthcare, finance, hospitality, and real estate.

Together, we operate as one collaborative ecosystem, combining deep expertise, AI-powered capabilities, and a culture of curiosity to help ambitious brands grow while creating meaningful opportunities for our people.

About the Role

As a Social Commerce Senior Coordinator, you will flex across affiliate management, UGC creator strategy, and live shopping support.

This is an entry-to-mid level role ideal for someone passionate about TikTok, creator culture, and performance marketing. You will work closely with senior strategists to execute, optimize, and scale social commerce programs.

You should be equal parts creative and analytical.

You should care about performance.

You should want to grow.

What you'll do

Affiliate Program Execution

  • Source and recruit creators aligned with brand positioning and funnel goals
  • Manage product seeding and creator communication
  • Track creator posting timelines and compliance
  • Monitor performance metrics (GMV, ROAS, CTR, CVR)
  • Surface weekly optimization opportunities

UGC Strategy & Creator Development

  • Assist in building creator shortlists based on campaign objectives
  • Contribute to creative briefs and hook development
  • Identify content trends and performance patterns
  • Track asset-level performance and recommend iteration paths
  • Support creator tiering and scaling strategies

Live Shopping Support

  • Assist in show prep and run-of-show development
  • Coordinate with hosts and moderators
  • Monitor live KPIs and engagement metrics
  • Contribute to post-live performance recaps and optimization recommendations

Reporting & Performance Analysis

  • Maintain tracking dashboards and reporting systems
  • Analyze creative and affiliate performance trends
  • Identify scaling opportunities
  • Contribute insights for internal and client discussions

What You Bring

  • 1–3 years experience in social media, influencer marketing, paid media, or e-commerce
  • Deep familiarity with TikTok and short-form content ecosystems
  • Strong written communication skills
  • Comfortable working inside spreadsheets and performance dashboards
  • Highly organized and deadline-oriented
  • Data-curious and performance-minded
  • Coachable and eager to grow
  • Thrives in fast-moving environments

Bonus if you have:

  • TikTok Shop experience
  • Affiliate platform experience
  • Experience briefing creators
  • Exposure to paid social testing
  • Experience in wellness, beauty, CPG, or fashion verticals

Why Join Us

You'll work alongside talented people who are passionate about solving problems, helping clients grow, and delivering meaningful results. We're a collaborative, fast-moving team where curiosity is encouraged, ideas are welcomed, and great work is recognized.

We believe the best work happens when people are trusted to take ownership, supported in their growth, and empowered to bring their unique perspectives to the table. Whether you're just getting started or bringing years of experience, you'll have the opportunity to make an impact while continuing to learn and grow.

Benefits & Compensation

We believe great people deserve great support. Our company offers competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, well-being, and career growth, including:

Competitive compensation

  • Flexible work environment
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • Unlimited paid time off
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Company-paid life and disability insurance
  • Paid parental leave
  • A collaborative culture with autonomy and ownership
  • Employee wellness programs and additional perks

Additional Information

No agencies, please.

We are proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels respected, valued, and empowered to succeed. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Please note that this job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be a comprehensive list of all responsibilities, duties, or qualifications, which may change based on business needs.

At this time, we are unable to sponsor or transfer employment visas for this position.

jobs.title: Senior Quantum Applications Engineer
jobs.excerpt: D-Wave Quantum Inc.  (NASDAQ: QBTS) is a leader in the development and delivery of quantum computing systems, software, and services.
jobs.description:
D-Wave Quantum Inc. (NASDAQ: QBTS) is a leader in the development and delivery of quantum computing systems, software, and services. It is the world’s first commercial supplier of quantum computers, and the first and only to offer dual-platform quantum computing products and services, spanning both annealing and gate-model quantum computing technologies. D-Wave’s mission is to help customers realize the value of quantum today through enterprise-grade systems available on-premises and via its Leap™ quantum cloud service, which offers 99.9% availability and uptime. More than 100 organizations across commercial, government, and research sectors trust D-Wave to address complex computational challenges using quantum computing. Learn more about realizing the value of quantum computing today and how D-Wave is shaping the quantum-driven industrial and societal advancements of tomorrow: .

About the role

We are seeking a talented Senior Quantum Applications Engineer to join our quantum applications and algorithms team. Our goal is to develop high-impact algorithms that will make our gate-model quantum systems valuable to users. We're searching for candidates who possess a robust technical background, particularly in developing quantum applications for fields such as chemistry, machine learning, and quantum error correction. The ideal candidate will not only bring substantial technical expertise to our diverse team but will also excel in facilitating clear communication across internal software, firmware, and hardware teams and with our users.

What you'll do

  • Collaborate with multiple research and engineering teams to design, implement, and rigorously test novel high-impact quantum applications in domains such as chemistry, materials science, machine learning, artificial intelligence, finance, and cryptography
  • Explore applications from post-NISQthrough tofault-tolerant commercial utility
  • Identifyalgorithms that enhance the value of our quantum hardware by considering its specific features and constraints
  • Implement and support simulation features
  • Work closely with quantum engineers to execute quantum applications on hardware

About You

  • MS or PhD in Physics, Chemistry, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mathematics, or related field with a specialization in quantum computing. Equivalent industry experience will also be considered
  • Minimum5+ years of experience in the development, simulation, and deployment of quantum algorithms including NISQ algorithms
  • Minimum3+ years of experience with Python programming or another general-purpose language, with a demonstratedtrack recordof shipping production-quality code
  • Expertisewith one or more quantum computing SDKs likeQiskit, PennyLane, or CUDA Quantum
  • Expertisewith principles of quantum computing and quantum information science
  • Demonstrated depth in at least oneapplication vertical(e.g., quantum chemistry, machine learning, finance, optimization, or cryptography), with hands-on project or product experience beyond coursework
  • Strong software engineering skills: writing clean, well-tested, maintainable code and collaborating through code review, version control, and CI/CD in a team environment
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted software development using LLM-based coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or ChatGPT Codex), including sound judgment about when to rely on their output and when to independently verify it
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with the ability to effectively communicate complex technical concepts

A D-Waver's DNA

  • We look at the future and say “why not”; we see possibilities where others see problems or routines. We show the way ahead and are committed to achieving ambitious goals.
  • We practice straight talk and listen generously to each other with empathy. We value different opinions and points of views. We ensure that we connect outside as well as inside to learn from others and inspire each other.
  • We hold ourselves accountable for delivering results. We make decisions & take responsibility so that we can act & support each other.
  • As leaders we motivate & engage our teams to undertake beyond what they originally thought possible, by developing our teams & creating the conditions for people to grow and empower themselves through enabling & coaching.

Our Compensation Philosophy is Simple but Powerful:

We believe providing D-Wavers with company ownership, competitive pay, and a range of meaningful benefits is the start of creating a culture where people want to give the best they’ve got — not because they’re simply making money, but because they’ve fallen in love with our vision, mission, values, and team.

During the interview process, your Recruiter will review our total rewards (base, equity, bonus, perks, benefit, culture) offerings. The final offer is determined by your proficiencies within this level.

Inclusion:

We celebrate diverse perspectives to drive innovation in our pursuit. Our employees range from distinguished domain experts with decades of experience in their respective fields, to bright and motivated graduates eager to make their mark. Our diverse and innovative team will make you feel appreciated, supported and empower your career growth at D-Wave.

The Fine Print:

No 3rd party candidates will be accepted

It is D-Wave policy to provide equal employment opportunity (EEO) to all persons regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, physical or mental disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state/provincial, local law.

The base pay range for this role is:

125,000 – 187,000 USD per year (New Haven)

jobs.title: Senior Coding/Revenue Integrity Analyst
jobs.excerpt: POSITION SUMMARY: Under the general direction of the Manager of Revenue Integrity, the Senior Coding and Revenue Integrity Analyst exists to ensure compliant charge capture and revenue tracking for both Boston Medical Center (BMC) and the professional Boston University Medical Group (BUMG) revenue.
jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY:

Under the general direction of the Manager of Revenue Integrity, the Senior Coding and Revenue Integrity Analyst exists to ensure compliant charge capture and revenue tracking for both Boston Medical Center (BMC) and the professional Boston University Medical Group (BUMG) revenue. Operating under limited supervision and working independently, this role monitors regulatory changes, payer requirements, and revenue integrity policies to support compliant coding and billing practices across the enterprise. The position functions as a critical analytical liaison across both hospital and professional billing environments, performing comprehensive reimbursement analysis and developing detailed resolution plans to mitigate institutional revenue leakage. This role drives cross-functional collaboration and fosters constructive relationships between clinical revenue-producing departments and core revenue cycle teams to proactively resolve workflow deficiencies.

Position: Senior Coding / Revenue Integrity Analyst

Department: Revenue Integrity

Location: Remote with the occasional need to visit onsite

ESSENTIAL RESPONSIBILITIES / DUTIES:

  • Revenue Cycle Initiative Leadership: Leads complex revenue cycle initiatives and large-scale optimization projects across high-revenue-generating or at-risk clinical departments to improve overall revenue integrity, operational efficiency, and regulatory compliance.

  • Project Work Plan Management: Develops and executes detailed project work plans, timelines, and resolution frameworks for complex, multi-departmental revenue initiatives with limited managerial oversight to ensure timely delivery of operational goals.

  • Epic System Workflow Validation: Monitors, audits, and validates active charging workflows within Epic and intersecting third-party charging interfaces to ensure technical baseline accuracy and appropriate system build configuration.

  • Root Cause Data Analysis: Analyzes Epic work queue data and revenue performance metrics to execute structural root cause analysis, identify localized workflow deficiencies, and present formalized interpretations and actionable findings to leadership.

  • Departmental Sourcing Support: Manages charging, coding, and billing processes within clinical departments by auditing revenue-producing activities to verify compliance with evolving government regulations and third-party payer contract requirements.

  • Cross-Functional Stakeholder Collaboration: Partners with departmental stakeholders, finance leaders, and revenue cycle teams to assess active clinical workflows, troubleshoot system issues, and deliver targeted training and analytical feedback.

  • Subject Matter Expertise & Escalation Support: Serves as the primary functional subject matter expert and institutional liaison for charge capture, supporting complex escalation issues and guiding cross-functional revenue cycle partners.

(The above statements in this job description are intended to depict the general nature and level of work assigned to the employee(s) in this job. The above is not intended to represent an exhaustive list of accountable duties and responsibilities required).

JOB REQUIREMENTS

REQUIRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Associate’s degree in Business, Healthcare, or a related field; and at least five (5) years of healthcare experience, including at least two years in an active role involving coding, auditing, finance, revenue cycle management, and/or physician billing (preferably within an Academic Medical Center setting); or equivalent combination of education and experience.

PREFERRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:

  • A Bachelor’s degree in Business, Healthcare Administration, or a closely related field, combined with five (5) or more years of progressive revenue integrity experience within a matrixed health system.

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS REQUIRED:

  • Certified Professional Coder (CPC), Certified Coding Specialist – Physician-based (CCS-P), or Certified Professional Medical Auditor (CPMA).

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES (KSAs):

  • Advanced Process and Root Cause Analysis: Advanced proficiency in process analysis, troubleshooting, and database investigation to structurally isolate billing deficiencies and engineer actionable solutions.

  • Healthcare Revenue Cycle Principles: Strong working knowledge of materials management, purchasing, contracting, and vendor management structures as they intersect with hospital charging systems, Epic, and nThrive applications.

  • Objective Data Synthesization: Advanced analytical skills to evaluate complex utilization datasets from multiple disparate sources, develop summary metrics, and translate findings into current, accurate procurement and billing recommendations.

  • Strategic Communication and Presentation: Superior written and verbal communication skills, including the objective ability to present complex fiscal trends, regulatory interpretations, and systemic recommendations to senior administrative and physician leadership.

  • Independent Project Management: Strong organizational and time management skills to manage deadlines, prioritize personal workloads, and autonomously drive multiple concurrent project plans.

  • Stakeholder Influence and Interviewing: Strong active listening and interviewing skills to gather relevant workflow data from clinical personnel and establish collaborative working relationships across diverse medical and administrative teams.

  • Office Application Competency: Intermediate to advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Forms, to execute automated operational reporting and project tracking.

Compensation Range:

$78,000.00- $113,000.00

This range offers an estimate based on the minimum job qualifications. However, our approach to determining base pay is comprehensive, and a broad range of factors is considered when making an offer. This includes education, experience, skills, and certifications/licensures as they directly relate to position requirements; as well as business/organizational needs, internal equity, and market-competitiveness. In addition, BMCHS offers generous total compensation that includes, but is not limited to, benefits (medical, dental, vision, pharmacy), discretionary annual bonuses and merit increases, Flexible Spending Accounts, 403(b) savings matches, paid time off, career advancement opportunities, and resources to support employee and family well-being.

NOTE: This range is based on Boston-area data, and is subject to modification based on geographic location.

Equal Opportunity Employer/Disabled/Veterans

According to the FTC, there has been a rise in employment offer scams. Our current job openings are listed on our website and applications are received only through our website. We do not ask or require downloads of any applications, or “apps” job offers are not extended over text messages or social media platforms. We do not ask individuals to purchase equipment for or prior to employment.
