Position Summary
DataSpring runs the largest healthcare data foundation in the U.S. The Sr. Data Engineer builds and owns the pipelines and data models behind our provider data platform and the ProView suite. You will spend most of your time writing production code on Azure Databricks and Azure SQL: ingesting provider data from many sources, modeling it with history and lineage, and deciding which source wins when they disagree. You will also own our data modeling standards and the automation that enforces them, and review the data model work of internal engineers and vendor delivery teams.

The Sr. Data Engineer is a full-time, remote, exempt position and reports to the Senior Director, Data Engineering & Architecture.

Specific Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate production pipelines on Azure Databricks and Azure SQL that ingest, integrate, and publish provider data from internal and third-party sources.
  • Design the data models those pipelines load, including integration and master-data layers with history (SCD Type 2), source lineage, and field-level survivorship rules.
  • Write production-grade SQL, PySpark, Python, and DDL, and tune performance and cost on large datasets.
  • Build data quality checks, reconciliation, monitoring, and alerting so problems surface before customers find them.
  • Own the data modeling and naming standards for SQL Server, Azure SQL, and Databricks (Delta Lake, Unity Catalog), and build the automated checks in Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines that enforce them.
  • Review data models, schema changes, and pull requests from internal engineers and vendor teams, and record modeling decisions so they can be traced later.
  • Maintain source-to-target mappings, data dictionaries, and ERDs, generated from the systems themselves wherever possible so they stay current.
  • Partner with Data Science, product, billing, and application teams to turn business requirements into data models and clear data contracts.
  • Protect PHI (Protected Health Information), including classification of sensitive columns, and maintain compliance with HIPAA, HITRUST, and SOC 2 audit requirements.

Supervisory Responsibilities

None. This role sets technical direction for internal engineers and vendor delivery teams without direct reports.

Skills

  • Expert SQL and strong PySpark and Python, with a track record of building and running production pipelines, not only designing them.
  • Deep relational and dimensional modeling skills, including history (SCD), entity resolution, and knowing when each approach is the wrong choice.
  • Hands-on experience with Azure Databricks: Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, medallion architecture, job orchestration (e.g., Databricks Asset Bundles), and performance tuning.
  • Git-based workflows and CI/CD in Azure DevOps or an equivalent platform, including database deployment automation with gated promotion across environments.
  • Experience with data quality testing and pipeline observability.
  • Ability to explain design decisions clearly to engineers, product owners, and leadership, and to hold a technical line with vendor teams while keeping the relationship productive.

Experience

Required:

  • 8+ years in data engineering, including at least 4 years designing data models that reached production at scale.
  • Recent, hands-on production engineering. You will be expected to write and ship code, not only review it.
  • Demonstrated experience building master data management, entity resolution, or survivorship logic across multiple data sources.
  • Experience defining data modeling standards and automating their enforcement.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Preferred:

  • Healthcare data experience, especially provider data, credentialing, or member eligibility data.
  • Experience reviewing or directing the work of vendor or offshore delivery teams.
  • Experience with data quality platforms (e.g., Ataccama) and data modeling tools (e.g., ER/Studio).
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools to build engineering automation.

Who We Are

jobs.description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.



About the Role

We are growing the team. As part of our FY28 plan, we are expanding our team of Cloud Security Specialist for Central Europe (CEUR). You would join at an early stage, help shape how the team works across the region, and have real influence over how we position, sell and win cloud security business.

The Cloud Security Specialist team strengthens CrowdStrike’s ability to grow, position, sell, and close cloud security business across EMEA. As a Cloud Security Specialist for Central Europe (CEUR), you will be the primary Falcon Cloud Security authority for your territories, working with enterprise customers across the region.

This is a cloud security specialist field sales role with two equally important engines. The first is your own: you will define and execute a business plan for your territories, build pipeline through direct outreach, and lead cloud security sales cycles from first conversation to close. The second is collaborative: you will work alongside CrowdStrike’s regional sales teams, helping them identify and win Falcon Cloud Security opportunities in their accounts. Your ability to make those colleagues more effective is as important as your ability to sell independently.

Must be based in DACH to be considered.


What You’ll Do

  • Define and execute a cloud security territory plan for your territories in Central Europe (CEUR): identifying high-potential accounts, prioritising based on fit and win potential, and holding yourself accountable to outcomes, not just activity.
  • Generate your own pipeline through direct outreach, insight-led engagement, partner collaboration, and marketing alignment. You will not wait for opportunities to come to you.
  • Lead Falcon Cloud Security sales cycles end to end: discovery, qualification, technical evaluation, business case, stakeholder alignment, and close.
  • Work closely with CrowdStrike’s regional sales teams: educating them on cloud security opportunities, joining strategic account conversations, and making Falcon Cloud Security a natural part of their account strategy. Your goal is to make them more successful, not to work around them.
  • Engage credibly at every level: from CISO and security leadership to DevOps and cloud architecture teams. You are technically confident enough to lead these conversations, with or without a solutions engineer in the room.
  • Help customers operationalise and consume Falcon Cloud Security products post-sale, contributing to renewal and expansion.
  • Stay current on CrowdStrike’s cloud security roadmap, cloud platform developments across AWS, Azure, and GCP, and the competitive landscape.
  • Provide product and market feedback to CrowdStrike’s product management and leadership teams.
  • Travel up to 50% to support customer engagement across your territories.

What You’ll Need

  • Minimum 5 years of enterprise technology sales experience with cloud security or cloud computing products.
  • A demonstrable track record of building your own pipeline: you have opened accounts that were not handed to you and can walk through exactly how you did it.
  • Experience working alongside and enabling generalist account teams: you know how to align with them, bring them into a cloud security strategy, and make them more effective without becoming dependent on them for leads.
  • Technical depth in cloud security: credible across cloud workload protection, container and Kubernetes security, cloud security posture management, and cloud detection and response. You can lead a technical conversation with confidence, whether or not a solutions engineer is present.
  • Commercial credibility at senior level: you have led conversations with CISOs, security leadership, and C-suite stakeholders, and closed complex enterprise deals in the €300K to €2M range.
  • Strong DACH and Eastern European market knowledge: existing relationships in the enterprise security ecosystem across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland , as well as Poland, the Czech Republic, and Romania, are strongly preferred.
  • Structured sales discipline: you use a qualification framework such as MEDDICC as a way of thinking, forecast accurately, and disqualify early when deals lack urgency, access, or committed champions.
  • Fluency in German and English.
  • Cloud practitioner certification (AWS, Azure, or GCP) preferred.
  • Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

Qualities of an Ideal Candidate

  • Owns their business: you have a plan, you work it, and you hold yourself accountable to results. You do not wait for someone to bring you a deal.
  • A natural collaborator who does not need to be the hero: regional sales teams want to work with you because you make them more successful, not because they have to.
  • Technically confident: you can go deep on cloud security architecture with a DevOps team and pivot to business impact with a CISO in the same conversation.
  • Commercially sharp: you qualify hard, forecast honestly, and know when to walk away.
  • Self-driven and organised: you manage a wide territory across multiple countries with structure and discipline.
  • Resilient and adaptable: you handle complex, long sales cycles and changing conditions without losing momentum.
  • Motivated to grow: curious about the market, the technology, and your own craft.

Benefits of Working at CrowdStrike:

  • Build and operate our Internal Developer Platform (IDP) — self-service provisioning portals, golden-path templates, CI/CD pipelines, and paved-road tooling that let engineering teams stand up environments without filing tickets.
  • Own platform and reliability outcomes — defining and managing service level indicators (SLIs), service level objectives (SLOs), and error budgets, and driving observability maturity across our cloud and hosted platforms.

jobs.description:
About Upstart

At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.

As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.

We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team:

At Upstart, our Applied AI team's mission is threefold:

  1. Agent Platform: Build and support the platform that makes it straightforward for non technical users across Upstart to build, launch, and operate AI agents (voice/chat/text) reliably.

  2. Borrower and Applicant Assistant Orchestration: Build the orchestration layer behind a unified personal assistant that shares context across specialized agents, giving applicants and borrowers a cohesive, assistant-like experience.

  3. Borrower-Connected Internal Workflows: Improve internal operational workflows that directly connect to applicant and borrower experiences, making them faster, smarter, and more efficient.

As Principal Engineer, LLM you will serve as a technical pathfinder and force multiplier for this team and the product squads we partner with. Rather than owning internal developer-tooling infrastructure or training foundation models from scratch, your mandate is to compress the time between an ambiguous idea and a reliable, user-facing AI system, while raising the applied AI bar across every squad you touch.

This role operates on an explicit 80/20 charter:

  • 0-to-1 Product and Architecture Pathfinder (~80%): Rapidly prototype high-ambiguity bets across our agent platform, cross-agent context orchestration, borrower-facing assistant experiences, and internal workflows. Partner directly with Product and Design to validate non-deterministic UX, establish clean architectural patterns, and hand off battle-tested evaluation contracts for engineering squads to scale.

  • AI-Native Engineering Catalyst (~20%): While dedicated internal teams own Upstart's broader AI developer tooling and software-factory initiatives, you will serve as a visible practitioner on the product side. You will lead by example with agentic coding workflows and tight verification harnesses, partner with our internal tooling teams as an early adopter ("customer zero"), and help product squads adopt higher-leverage ways of working.

Because AI systems are non-deterministic, user experience is part of the architecture. Whether you are designing cross-agent handoffs, borrower-facing assistant flows, or internal operational tools, you will navigate real-world trade-offs across latency, unit economics, reliability, and user trust, and push back constructively when a simpler deterministic approach is the right call.

How you’ll make an impact

  • De-risk 0-to-1 bets across the stack: Rapidly prototype ambiguous initiatives spanning multi-agent context sharing, UX for non technical users, platform primitives for launching agents, and borrower-connected internal workflows.

  • Deliver durable evaluation contracts, not throwaway handoffs: Treat prototype code as disposable proof of concept, and hand off to engineers what they actually need to build production services with confidence: golden datasets, automated evaluation harnesses, documented failure-mode maps, latency/cost benchmarks, and clean architectural blueprints.

  • Partner cleanly from spike to production: Align early with receiving squad tech leads to surface system constraints, support joint go/no-go decisions with Engineering and Product leadership (including killing unviable bets early), and stay engaged through initial productionization to review early PRs and debug edge-case model behavior.

  • Design non-deterministic UX and orchestration together: Treat latency spikes, context loss between agents, subtle hallucinations, and fallback paths as systems design problems, shaping experiences that earn and protect borrower and operator trust.

  • Make pragmatic applied AI trade-offs: Default to the simplest reliable solution first (prompting, context engineering, deterministic guardrails), and make clear architectural calls on model routing, fine-tuning, or distillation when latency, unit economics, or reliability require it.

  • Raise the applied AI bar across squads: Model disciplined agentic coding and verification practices in your daily workflow, feed practical requirements back to internal tooling teams, and elevate engineering judgment across teams through active collaboration.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Software engineering foundation and live AI shipping: 8+ years of software engineering experience, along with hands-on experience shipping non-deterministic, user-facing LLM or AI products to real users.

  • Agentic and LLM systems architecture: Deep practical experience designing production LLM systems involving structured outputs, tool calling, context engineering, retrieval/memory patterns, and multi-step or multi-agent orchestration (including state management and context sharing across agents).

  • Production systems, latency, and reliability engineering: Strong distributed-systems and backend fundamentals for non-deterministic pipelines: async orchestration, streaming UX, caching, timeouts and fallback paths, rate-limit handling, and end-to-end observability/tracing to diagnose failures.

  • Evaluation and quality engineering: Proven experience building golden datasets, automated evaluation harnesses (deterministic checks, heuristics, and LLM-as-a-judge), regression gates, and systematic failure-mode analyses.

  • Safety, guardrails, and applied AI pragmatism: Strong instinct to reach for the simplest reliable tool first (deterministic logic, prompting, context engineering, guardrails against hallucinations and prompt/data risks), paired with sound judgment on when latency, unit cost, or reliability justify routing, fine-tuning, or distillation over frontier APIs.

  • Full-stack prototyping fluency: Comfortable moving fast across backend and frontend stacks (such as Python, TypeScript/React, and modern REST or streaming APIs) to put working end-to-end prototypes in front of users and stakeholders quickly.

  • Low-ego pathfinder collaboration and UX empathy: Track record aligning early with partner squads, handing off ownership cleanly without ego, and partnering directly with Product, Design, and operations or business leaders to turn ambiguous goals into concrete latency budgets and resilient fallback experiences.

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Startup or 0-to-1 incubation DNA: Experience operating in early-stage or low-boundary environments where you owned ambiguous problems end to end under real constraints.

  • Agent platform and shared abstractions: Experience designing reusable agent primitives, SDKs, or orchestration platforms that help peer engineering teams build, evaluate, and launch AI workflows safely and quickly.

  • Production fine-tuning and distillation reps: Hands-on experience fine-tuning or distilling smaller models in production to improve latency, unit economics, or task reliability.

  • AI-native engineering habits: Deep daily fluency with agentic coding workflows and automated verification harnesses, plus experience helping peer engineers adopt higher-leverage development practices.

  • Experience in regulated or high-trust consumer domains (such as fintech, lending, or healthcare) where accuracy, explainability, PII protection, and user trust are critical.

Position location This role is available in the following locations: Remote

Time zone requirements The team operates on the East/West coast time zones.

Travel requirements As a digital first company, the majority of your work can be accomplished remotely. The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S but are encouraged to to still spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites. The in-person sessions’ cadence varies depending on the team and role; most teams meet once or twice per quarter for 2-4 consecutive days at a time.

At Upstart, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. The anticipated base salary for this position is expected to be within the below range. The project and the team

As the software keeps expanding and becoming a fully-fledged product, we're looking for another Senior Frontend Engineer to help build what's next. It is as much a product engineering challenge as a technical one.

Other things to know:

  • The team consists of Software and DevOps engineers who share strong ownership of code and product quality

  • AI tools are part of the daily workflow

Your role

  • Designing and building multi-step micro-apps and shared UI libraries in a React and TypeScript monorepo

  • Modelling long-running, asynchronous workflows in the UI: progress, polling, cancel, retry and recovery after a page reload

  • Evolving shared frontend foundations: pure TypeScript workflow state machines, micro-frontend boundaries and reusable accessible components

  • Keeping the application fast on very large datasets (100k+ items), including profiling, virtualisation and performance budgets

  • Writing unit, reducer, component and browser/E2E tests (Vitest, React Testing Library, Storybook, Playwright) running in CI (GitLab CI)

  • Applying AI-assisted engineering practices and setting the standard for how they are used - across the entire SDLC, not only in code generation

  • Contributing to architecture and design decisions as the solution scales in different dimensions

  • Proposing and helping ship your own ideas for improving the product, beyond your core delivery work

Do we have a match?

As a Senior Software Engineer, you must meet the following criteria:

  • Strong, 7+ years professional experience in similar roles

  • Experience building and maintaining software products for external customers

  • Languages / Frontend: TypeScript, JavaScript, React (micro-frontends)

  • Build & monorepo tooling: Vite, pnpm, Turborepo, Storybook, Oxlint

  • State management, forms & data fetching: TanStack Query, React Hook Form, Zod, Context API, state machines / reducers

  • Hands-on, everyday use of AI coding tools in your engineering workflow, with a considered view of where they earn their keep and where they do not

  • CI/CD experience

  • Comfortable in a fast-paced environment where priorities are set as much by customers as by the backlog

  • Open for technical challenges

Beyond the criteria above, we would appreciate the following:

  • Experience with micro-frontend architectures

  • Experience with Connect-RPC, gRPC-Web or Protobuf

  • Experience with client-side observability

More reasons to join us

  • Professional growth supported by internal training sessions and a training budget

En idealista, estamos buscando un Android Product Engineer para nuestro equipo de tecnología.

¿Qué harás?

  • Trabajarás integrado en un journey de producto, con responsabilidad real sobre las funcionalidades de tu área: desde entender el problema con PM y UX hasta verlo en manos de los usuarios.

  • Usarás herramientas de IA de forma habitual en tu proceso de trabajo: desde acelerar tareas de desarrollo hasta mejorar la calidad de lo que entregas.

  • También tendrás bugs, legacy code y decisiones técnicas difíciles. Eso no cambia.

¿Qué esperamos de ti?

Esto es lo que más nos importa:

  • Tienes experiencia real trabajando en un entorno orientado a producto: has participado en decisiones, no solo en ejecución.

  • Te comunicas bien: con compañeros de equipo, con PM, con QA, con UX. Preguntas, explicas, escalas cuando toca, y lo haces de forma que la gente entiende y confía.

  • Eres capaz de gestionar varios frentes a la vez sin perder contexto: sabes priorizar, pedir ayuda cuando procede y mantener visibilidad sobre lo que tienes en marcha.

  • Usas IA de manera natural en tu día a día, no como experimento: para desarrollar más rápido, revisar código, explorar alternativas, documentar, o lo que encuentres útil en tu flujo de trabajo.

  • Tienes criterio propio: no solo ejecutas lo que te dicen, también propones, cuestionas y defiendes tus argumentos.

Técnicamente:

  • Kotlin es tu lenguaje principal y Android tu entorno habitual.

  • Conoces las buenas prácticas del desarrollo Android moderno y las aplicas, aunque no seas purista.

  • Puedes leer y trabajar con código legacy sin que te paralice.

¿Qué otras cosas son un plus?

  • Sensibilidad por la parte de UI y experiencia trabajando con sistemas de diseño.

  • Experiencia con apps multi-módulo a gran escala.

  • Has trabajado con pipelines de CI/CD.

  • Tienes experiencia con marcaje de eventos (Piano, Tealium).

  • Te interesan otras plataformas o disciplinas: iOS, backend, data analytics.

  • Has hecho algo con tecnologías multiplataforma (KMP, React Native).

  • Entiendes el testing y lo valoras como parte del trabajo, no como trámite.

¿Qué te ofrecemos?

  • Podrás ver el impacto directo de tu trabajo en una de las apps de referencia tanto en España, como en Italia, Portugal y Francia. Para los que no lo hayáis vivido ya: no sabéis el cosquilleo que da en la tripa la primera vez que ves algo que has hecho en una plataforma que utilizan millones de personas.

  • Somos Remote Friendly :) pero tenemos oficinas en el centro de Madrid por si te apetece venir algún día y en otros puntos de España.

  • Vas a aprender. Lo decimos en serio. La plataforma va evolucionando constantemente, y de ahí sacamos mogollón de charlas internas, posts, talleres… que hacen que el conocimiento fluya.

  • Además... patrocinamos eventos, acudimos a ellos y hacemos muchos meetups. ¡Es tan importante aprender como enseñar a tus compis!

  • Además de tu salario, podrás acogerte a un plan de retribución flexible (tarjeta de transporte, cheques gourmet, seguro médico…) del que te podrás beneficiar desde el primer día.

  • Clases de Inglés, italiano y portugués.

  • Fruta fresca y café siempre disponible en la cocina.

  • ¡También tenemos fisio y clases de yoga … porque para nosotros lo más importante es cuidar de nuestros idealistas!

  • Además de trabajar, nos gusta pasarlo bien, por eso que si te unes a nuestras familia, cada mes celebrarás algo…Halloween, San Valentín, Navidad,…¡Te lo vas a pasar muy bien! Teambuilding y mucho más!

Y algo más sobre nosotros...

Desde que iniciamos esta aventura en el año 2000, idealista es mucho más que una compañía.

Es una cultura, una forma de hacer y entender las cosas que nos diferencia. El respeto, la tolerancia, la integridad y la transparencia forman parte de nuestro ADN.

Contamos con un equipo de personas que representa a más de 20 nacionalidades distintas, con idiomas diversos, perfiles, culturas y orígenes diferentes. Valoramos la diferencia y aprender de los demás; diferentes creencias y formas de pensar nos enriquecen.

idealista fomenta la igualdad en todos los ámbitos, realizando acciones de sensibilización y visibilidad del colectivo LGTB+ entre los empleados/as, en la publicidad y en la comunidad en general.

Tenemos el compromiso de crear entornos y espacios donde las personas se sientan seguras, protegidas, libres de discriminación y primando la igualdad de oportunidades.

Asimismo, la promoción de la igualdad de género es otra de las bases de nuestro compromiso con nuestro equipo. Estamos comprometidos con el desarrollo de medidas que fomenten la igualdad y favorezcan la conciliación, maternidad y paternidad.

Estamos deseando conocerte y que nos conozcas.

jobs.description:
As a Forward Deployed Engineer at Leena AI, you will embed directly with our most strategic enterprise customers to drive transformational AI adoption in HR, IT, and Operations. You will collaborate closely with customer teams to ship advanced AI applications—AI Colleagues, workflow automations, and enterprise integrations—that solve real-world business problems. This is not just a spec-writing role. You are in the field, inside the client’s environment, building and deploying production systems that move organizations from manual processes to AI-powered automation at scale.

The Forward Deployed Engineer owns technical delivery end-to-end of our most challenging customers. You'll gather requirements directly from the client, design the integration blueprint, align stakeholders on the approach, and then build it—writing production code, configuring the platform, and connecting enterprise systems. Beyond go-live, you continue to own the deployment: troubleshooting issues, evolving the implementation as client needs change, and serving as the technical point of contact through the lifetime of the account. Working closely with our Post-Sales, Product, and Engineering teams, you'll partner with engineers to unblock complex problems and feed real-world learnings back into the product. As one of our early FDEs, you'll help shape Leena AI's go-to-market motion. We expect our FDEs to operate autonomously, thrive under ambiguity, and represent Leena AI at the highest level in customer environments.

What We’re Looking ForOur customer conversations are 90% technical. We need one person who brings three things together—and that person is rare.

  • Platform Mastery. You go deep on the Leena AI platform—fast. Within weeks, you can configure it, build on top of it, and push it to its limits inside a customer's environment without waiting for someone to tell you what's possible.
  • Integration Expertise. Integrations are the highest-risk element of every enterprise deployment. You own and mitigate this risk. You navigate customer APIs, access constraints, and messy enterprise environments and get integrations live anyway.
  • Customer Ownership. You control the room. You operate consultatively, adapt without a playbook, and build the trust that makes customers believe Leena AI is the right partner. You don’t need a PM to run point—you are the point.

Key Responsibilities
Integration Build & Execution

  • Design integration blueprints and solution architectures directly with the client, then own the hands-on execution—translating your designs into working systems without losing fidelity to agreed scope.
  • Prototype custom integrations, API connectors, and workflow automation in Python, TypeScript, and JavaScript across enterprise systems including Workday, ServiceNow, SAP, Oracle, and UKG.
  • Build and configure AI Colleagues, Agent Operating Procedures (AOPs), and Skills directly inside the client's environment—working within their systems, security constraints, and timelines.
  • Navigate real-world enterprise constraints—SSO/SAML/OIDC, legacy HRIS, data residency, and IT security gatekeeping—to get integrations across the finish line.
  • Author Solution Design Documents (SDDs) with precision—flagging scope gaps or technical blockers early and looping in PMs or Engineering before they hit the client timeline.
  • Identify non-standard requirements early and align internal engineering resources to close gaps before they block delivery.
  • Own the 2-week hypercare period post go-live, ensuring stability and rapid resolution of any production issues.

Enterprise Integration & Platform Expertise

  • Understand and configure end-to-end integrations with HRIS, ITSM, payroll, and directory systems using REST APIs, webhooks, and out-of-box Leena AI connectors.
  • Understand and configure complex authentication flows including OAuth 2.0, SAML, and API key management across client enterprise environments.
  • Build and validate test cases for both internal UAT and client UAT, ensuring quality before go-live.
  • Debug and resolve 400/500-series API errors, integration failures, and platform configuration issues with urgency and precision.

Client Partnership & Escalation Management

  • Serve as the senior technical point of contact for enterprise clients during active implementations, participating in steering committees and technical working sessions.
  • Act as a technical escalation resource for the broader Professional Services team—triaging issues, unblocking SCs and PMs, and providing authoritative answers to client technical questions.
  • Proactively communicate risks, dependencies, and blockers to PMs and leadership before they become CIO-level escalations.
  • Participate in pre-call readiness reviews to ensure no client-facing question goes unanswered.

Knowledge Sharing & Team Enablement

  • Identify and codify repeatable integration patterns from each deployment—building a library of reusable templates, connector configurations, and self-serve documentation that accelerates future FDE engagements.

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.excerpt: We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production.
jobs.description:
We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable.

Our stack is Python (FastAPI) on AWS, with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows.

Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD.

What You Will Do:

  • Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end.

  • Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails.

  • Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production.

  • Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

  • Drive the full software development lifecycle, translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans.

What We Are Looking For:

  • 5+ years building and operating production backend systems, with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end.

  • Deep fluency in your primary backend language, and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly.

  • Strong systems fundamentals — concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes — and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one.

  • Sound reasoning under ambiguity: you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change.

  • Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations, including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar).

  • Professional written English, enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs.

Even Better:

  • AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience.

  • Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions.

  • A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal.

How We Hire:

We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build:

  • 1. A 120-minute conversation focusing on your background and a collaborative system-design exercise and cultural fit..

  • 2. A 120-minute live technical session involving code review, live coding, and a self-review.

You may complete the technical session in your strongest language (Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, or TypeScript/Node.js). Web search is encouraged; AI assistants are not used. We want to see your fundamental engineering judgment.

What We Offer:

  • Competitive USD-based salary and a comprehensive benefits package.

  • Hybrid work flexibility with hours that support deep work.

  • The opportunity to work at the frontier of agentic AI, tackling hard problems with high ownership.

  • A highly educated, agile senior team that values pragmatism, learning, and continuous improvement.

If you would rather be judged on how you think than on a buzzword list, we would like to talk!
